meta.title: Row-level verification, 2026-11-14 (session arena/428e6264-nba1)
meta.method: Every published value listed here was re-read from an NBA-operated page in this session and compared to the value the repository publishes. A row is VERIFIED only when the two agree exactly. UNVERIFIED means no official read confirmed it this session. MISMATCH means the official read and the published value disagree. The evidence URL and the retrieval time are recorded per row.
meta.not_used: No third-party site (no sportsbook, no aggregator, no ESPN, no news outlet) was used to confirm any value.
limits: This sandbox cannot open a raw socket to *.nba.com (curl reports SSL_ERROR_SYSCALL); reads are made through the agent's web-fetch tool, which does reach the official hosts. Latency and byte counts are therefore not available here.
A page that returns unrendered content (scores shown as '-') is recorded as not-readable for that date, never as verified.
Where the official page shows a value that moves during the day (injury designations, season averages), the read timestamp is part of the claim and the row says so.

rows.check: Re-derivation of the originated spread for DEN@NOP from the repo's own published constants
rows.detail: smoothed win pct = (W+3)/(G+6); margin = 35 x (p_home - p_away) + 2.5; spread = -round_half(margin)
rows.repo_value: DEN 6-4, NOP 4-8 -> expected margin -3.6, originated spread +3.5, DEN -3.5, p(home win) 0.419
rows.official_value: independent recomputation from the published formula gives -3.576, +3.5, 0.4194 — identical after rounding
rows.note: This is a code-plus-input check, not a fact about the world: it proves the published number is the number the published formula produces from the published records. Whether the formula is any good is a separate question (see V-09).
rows.result: Independent recomputation reproduces the published spread and win probability after rounding.

rows.check: Every p-value, Wilson bound and luck decomposition the site publishes

rows.check: Multiple-testing correction across the six strategies that have graded plays
rows.detail: Benjamini-Hochberg on the six two-sided p-values vs a coin flip
rows.repo_value: no corrected q-value is published anywhere in the repository
rows.official_value: BH q for S1 = 0.120; every other strategy q >= 0.998
rows.status: NEW FINDING (not published by the repo)
rows.note: The site's headline is that S1 cleared the luck gate at p=0.020. Across six strategies tested, the corrected q is 0.120, i.e. it does not survive. This does not make S1 wrong; it makes the headline stronger than the statistics support. Flagged F-05.
rows.result: BH q = 0.120 for S1; every other strategy q >= 0.998.

rows.check: Is S1's edge size related to its win rate (i.e. is it a skill gradient)?
rows.detail: Split S1's 32 picks at the median |model - reference| of 5.70 points
rows.official_value: small-edge half 11/16 (0.688), large-edge half 12/16 (0.750); point-biserial r = 0.051
rows.note: A skill signal should strengthen as the disagreement grows. It barely does (r=0.05 on n=32). This is the cleanest available argument that S1's record may be luck rather than signal. Flagged F-05.
rows.result: 11/16 vs 12/16 across the median split; r = 0.051.

rows.check: The fitted home-court advantage, back-to-back penalty and residual sigma
rows.detail: hca 3.51, b2b penalty 6.26, sigma_margin 17.41, sigma_total 19.68 (site build)
rows.official_value: residuals recomputed from the 60 stored forecasts: bias -0.167 (published -0.17), MAE 12.977 (12.98), sigma 17.12 population / 17.26 sample (published 17.41)
rows.note: MAE and bias reproduce exactly. The published sigma 17.41 is 0.15-0.29 above what the stored residuals give, depending on the estimator; the repository does not print which estimator it uses, so the difference cannot be closed from here. Flagged F-08 (minor, no published decision depends on it).
rows.result: MAE and bias reproduce; sigma does not reproduce to the published precision.

rows.check: Two builds report different error statistics for the same 60 games
rows.detail: Site build (validation.json) vs Integration Desk (settlement.json)
rows.repo_value: validation.json: MAE margin 12.98, MAE total 14.83. settlement.json: MAE margin 12.913, MAE total 14.636
rows.official_value: both are internally consistent; recomputation from settlement.json rows gives 12.913 and 14.636 exactly, and from backtest.json rows gives 12.977 and 14.830
rows.note: Not an arithmetic error — two different forecast series over the same 60 games. But nothing on either page tells the reader that the other exists. Flagged F-09.
rows.result: Two internally consistent, different numbers for the same 60 games.

rows.check: The seven gates and whether any strategy has passed all seven
rows.detail: G1 sample, G2 calibration, G3 break-even, G4 luck, G5 stability, G6 correlation, G7 (market/price)
rows.repo_value: no strategy is funded; S1 passes G1/G3/G4 and fails G2 and G5
rows.official_value: not checkable against an official source — it is the repository's own rule
rows.note: Recorded because the brief asks for validation gates: the gate machinery is real and is applied honestly here. The missing gate is G7 — no NBA-operated price exists, so no strategy can ever be shown to beat a market. That is the central open question, not a bug.
rows.result: Gates are defined and applied; G7 cannot run because no price source exists.
